newsitem.title: USA: Romania presses to join NATO in U.S. talks.
newsitem.headline: Romania presses to join NATO in U.S. talks.

text.p: Romanian Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea met U.S. Vice President Al Gore on Wednesday to press his country's case for membership in an expanded NATO.

After the White House meeting, Ciorbea told reporters Romania would "fight to the very end" to be included in the first round of new members to be invited to enter the Western security alliance at next month's NATO summit in Madrid.

The 16-member North Atlantic Treaty Organisation paved the way to its eastward expansion last month when President Bill Clinton, Russian President Boris Yeltsin and the other alliance members signed the "NATO-Russia Founding Act" to chart future relations.

The United States has said it favours inviting only the Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland to join NATO in the first round, a position at odds with an effort by France, Italy and others to include Romania and Slovenia in the first wave.
Since the alliance operates by consensus, the Clinton administration is confident its stance will prevail.
Romania, strategically positioned near the Balkans and the Black Sea, was "an exporter of stability even now when we are not a member of NATO," Ciorbea said.

He couched his country's refusal to take a U.S. "no" for an answer on a first round NATO invitation in diplomatic terms. Ciorbea said he had told Gore it was Romania's desire to "solve the problem and not to create new problems."
U.S. policymakers have said the first new members of NATO will not be the last, and Washington has hinted that Romania and Slovenia will be next in line.
But Ciorbea said Gore was "not able to fix a date" for the next phase of NATO expansion, saying this would have to be decided by the alliance as a whole.
